summary: 1933 Civilian Conservation Corps fire tower on Bickle Knob in Monongahela National Forest; cab removed for a public viewing platform, tower still standing and open.

facts.status_note: The tower still stands, but its fire observer's cab has been removed and replaced with an open viewing platform.

access.note: Open wooden viewing platform for public use, per the Gazette-Mail; the Wikipedia article says the tower is not handicapped-accessible.

visit.trail_note: Easily accessible during warm-weather months (Wikipedia). A Forest Service sign along Stuart Memorial Drive northeast of Elkins marks the approach. Not handicap-accessible.

events.note: Built by Civilian Conservation Corps workers, per the Register and the Gazette-Mail; Forest Lookouts cites a Monongahela National Forest history for CCC labor
Charleston Gazette item of August 27, 1934, quoted by Forest Lookouts, describes the tower as one of a series of similar towers built to protect the forest from fire
Registered January 3, 2015 as US 1101, WV 12; nominated by Brian Powell
NHLR visit report dated March 5, 2017 records the tower as not staffed and in good condition; stairs OK

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Register gives the summit as 4,012 ft (1,223 m). The Gazette-Mail calls the observation tower 4,004 feet high. The story gives the Register figure and says the sources disagree.

The Register calls the change an open viewing deck; the Gazette-Mail and Wikipedia call it a wooden viewing platform. These are the same structure, so the story uses the platform wording and cites all three.

sources.title: Land Trust transfers Bickle Knob land to Monongahela Forest

notes_for_editor: Brief record checked: the 1933 build, 2015 NHLR registration, elevation and coordinates match the sources. Brief status note (cab gone) is supported by the FFLOS asterisk legend and the Register. The brief's access 'unknown' is now public (open platform). Decommissioning is dated only to the 1960s by the Gazette-Mail, so no closed event is recorded. Not used: a 2022 personal blog (stillsheroams.com) that says staffing was phased out by the 1970s; it conflicts in date with the Gazette-Mail's 1960s decommissioning and was not fetched or quoted. The Register's photo credits (1933 National Archives photo, Oct 2010 Brian Powell photo, 2017 Kristin Reynolds photo) have no image URLs here, so no photos were recorded. The first WebSearch returned the Register, Wikipedia and Gazette-Mail snippets; they were checked against fetched text before use.
